newVariant.name: Crest trail north from Harts Pass to the border monument, then cross-country to Crow Creek basin
newVariant.season: Jul-Sep; the Harts Pass road usually opens in July, and snow on north-facing trail can linger to mid-Aug
newVariant.notes:
The other way in that stays inside the United States. It takes you directly under the north face rather than to the far side of the peak, and it is very long.

Drive to Harts Pass on the rough upper road (high clearance recommended) and walk the crest trail north for about 30 miles to the northern terminus monument at the border. You cannot continue into Canada from there; the monument is where the lawful walk ends.

From the monument area, cross Castle Creek on the trail bridge just south of the boundary rather than fording at the swath. Then traverse south-west for about 3 miles through brushy forest choked with deadfall: cross Princess Creek around 5,100 ft, climb to about 5,600 ft and contour into the Crow Creek drainage. The lower basin is swampy and buggy. Camp higher, in the upper basin below the face, so you are on the glacier the next morning.

A free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead. Check with the Methow Valley Ranger District for road, snow and fire closures before committing to it.
hazards: Roughly thirty miles of trail each way before the cross-country starts
Brushy, deadfall-choked traverse from the border to the basin
Castle Creek is not a casual ford near the boundary
Snow on north-facing trail slopes can be hazardous before mid-August
Water can be far apart along the crest trail
Swampy, mosquito-heavy lower Crow Creek basin
The boundary is close the whole way; do not walk into Canada
Retreat from the face is measured in days
newVariant.baseFinding: The traverse ends in Crow Creek basin directly below the north face. From a camp in the upper basin, climb the moraine to the glacier. The wall, and how you pick out the route on it, are the same as from any other approach.

wa_castle_peak_pasayten_the_drawbridge.why: Primary = v0 (Ross Lake/Freezeout). The paragraph describes v1 (Frosty/Crow Creek from Lightning Lake, the first-ascent line). I applied the lawful-only rule. Evidence that recent ascents come from Manning Park, an unlawful cross-country entry: stevensong.com/usa/washington/castle-peak-pasayten-wa (June 2023, via Frosty East); mountainproject.com/area/106464644 'Getting There' (Frosty lookout, 'over international border'); alpinist.com 2008 Fight or Flight first ascent from Manning; onehikeaweek.com 2016 via Monument 78. The most-used LAWFUL approach is Ross Lake boat + Lightning Creek + Freezeout Creek (v0). Source 1: lemkeclimbs.com/castle-peak.html, Oct 2023 ascent (boat, Lightning Creek TH, Freezeout cabin at 3,600 ft, tread gone at ~4,200 ft). It says the Ross Lake water taxi books out months ahead because the Nov-2021 floods damaged the Canadian access. Source 2: stevensong.com says 'the way that completely stays within U.S. requires an expensive boat ride across Ross Lake', i.e. it treats Ross Lake as THE all-US approach. I found NO documented ascent via the PCT from Harts Pass, so the PCT is not 'most used'. A lawful PCT approach is real and is named as an option: wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/castle-peak ('the PCT'), and SummitPost p.295595 via a search snippet ('another approach from the east (from the Pacific Crest Trail)'). These two may share an author. Sources for the facts in the optional newVariant: the FS Harts Pass TH page (typically accessible July-Sep; FR 5400 rugged, high clearance); the Mountaineers PCT Harts Pass->Manning Park page via a search snippet (~30 mi north on the PCT; water sources far apart; north-slope snow treacherous before mid-August); WTA historic trip report tripreport-2004070307 (from Monument 78: Castle Creek hard to cross at the swath, crossed on the PCT bridge; SW traverse ~3 mi through brush and deadfall; Princess Creek at 5,100 ft; contour at 5,600 ft into Crow Creek; lower basin a mosquito swamp; camp at 5,600 ft in the upper basin under the north face). The newVariant is OPTIONAL and NOT primary. Add it only if you want the existing notes' reference to a 'crest trail' lawful alternative to point at a listed variant. Those notes call it 'from the west'; it actually comes in from the east. PCT bridge condition in 2026 is unverified. Also, WTA shows the Castle Peak and Castle Pass trails CLOSED for the 2026 Ptarmigan Fire (notices 7.31.26 and 9.14.26). That closure is temporary and is not written into the variant.

wa_north_face_left_buttress.why: Primary = v0 (Ross Lake/Freezeout). The paragraph describes both ways in: Canada, which it calls 'the more common approach', and the US side. Same peak and same evidence as wa_castle_peak_pasayten_the_drawbridge. Recent ascents come from Manning Park, an unlawful cross-country entry (stevensong 2023; Mountain Project 'Getting There'; this route's own 2008 first ascent drove in via Manning, per alpinist.com). The most-used lawful approach is Ross Lake + Freezeout (lemkeclimbs.com Oct 2023; stevensong.com calls Ross Lake the only all-US way). I found no documented ascent via the PCT from Harts Pass. The optional PCT newVariant is sourced as described in the Drawbridge entry (FS Harts Pass page; Mountaineers PCT page; WTA 2004 trip report tripreport-2004070307 for the Monument 78 -> Crow Creek traverse). It is not primary.

wa_clark_mountain_west_ridge.why: The route itself is 'West Ridge / Walrus Glacier' (mountaineering). Every recent climbing report I found goes Boulder Basin -> Boulder Pass -> Walrus Glacier: WTA trip report 2024-09-03 ('White River, Boulder Pass, Clark Mountain'); Mountaineers 'Basic Glacier Climb - Clark Mountain/Walrus Glacier' reports (2022 and Aug 2024, via search snippets); trailcatjim.com Oct 2023 ('Clark Mtn via Boulder Basin-Walrus Glacier-East Ridge'); NWHikers 2019 ('Clark Mountain - Boulder Pass/Walrus Glacier'); Wenatchee Outdoors. The non-glacier sheepherder line (v0) is listed separately by the Mountaineers as the 'Clark Mountain/Southeast Route' ALPINE SCRAMBLE, a different route for a different kind of party. So the old 'Walrus is not the most common route' line most likely refers to scramblers. The route's own timing block also follows the Walrus line. The paragraph describes both lines from Boulder Basin.

wa_mount_rainier_ptarmigan_ridge.why: This is no longer only a seasonal question. The SR165/Fairfax Bridge was permanently closed on 22 Apr 2025. NPS states there is NO public access to Carbon River and Mowich Lake: the road is closed to vehicles, bikes AND pedestrians, with no alternate route (https://www.nps.gov/mora/planyourvisit/carbon-river-and-mowich.htm). Coverage of the WSDOT planning study puts restored access no earlier than ~2031. So Mowich Lake (v0) is unavailable in every season, and White River/St Elmo/Curtis Ridge (v1) is the only way in that a car can reach. Recent reports use v1: CascadeClimbers 'Rainier Roundup 2025' (includes Ptarmigan Ridge); Mountaineers Ptarmigan reports going White River CG (4,400 ft) -> lower Curtis Ridge (7,500 ft) -> Ptarmigan high camp (10,300 ft). Even before 2025, the route's May-June season came before the July Mowich opening. The paragraph describes both and frames the choice as seasonal. FOLLOW-UP for caller: v0's season text and notes ('summer-only road that opens well after...') and the paragraph are now stale and misleading, because the road is closed indefinitely, not seasonally. Suggested v0 season: 'May-Jul; the road to Mowich Lake is closed indefinitely, so this start cannot currently be reached by car'.

wa_trapper_mountain_south_slopes.why: WTA trip report, Sep 2023 (trip_report.2024-03-11.2795822533): the hiker came from Stehekin, tried the Old Cottonwood route ('sketchy and impossible to find'), and found 'the most-used route from Pelton Basin'. WTA trip report, Sep 2019 (trip_report.2019-09-20.9009301980): Cascade Pass TH -> Pelton Basin -> saddle -> steep alder descent to the lake, ~10 h. It calls reaching the outlet side from Cottonwood extremely difficult. The route's own timing block is written for Cascade Pass/Pelton Basin, and v1's 5,392 ft pass is Cascade Pass. v0 (ferry + Harlequin) is far longer and its own notes flag conflicting drainages. The paragraph describes v0. Caveat for caller: v1's season text says 'Late spring into summer', but the Cascade River Road to the trailhead typically opens around early July. Not changed here.

wa_mount_ballard_south.why: Several independent sources, some recent, call Slate Creek THE standard way up Ballard. countryhighpoints.com/mount-ballard (Oct 2018): 'The standard way to climb Mt Ballard is to drive over Harts Pass down Slate Creek... scramble up the east face, and finish on the west face'. countryhighpoints.com/mt-ballard-survey (2025): 'The standard route on Mt Ballard is to climb the east face starting at Slate Creek'. stevensong.com/usa/washington/mount-ballard: 'standard, East Face route'. lemkeclimbs.com/mount-ballard.html: Slate Creek gate at 3,800 ft -> South Fork bridge at 4,000 ft. trailcatjim.com: Slate Creek-East Ridge. The Mill Creek/Azurite ascents I found (v0) are older (onehikeaweek 2012; drdirtbag and WTA 2016), and that trail is badly overgrown. The paragraph describes v0 and mentions the West Fork Methow alternate. CAVEAT for caller: this route is named 'South Slopes', and v0 is the approach that reaches the south flank; v1 reaches the summit by the east face/ridge. If the badge means 'most-used way to this summit', v1 is right. If it must be the way to the south slopes specifically, use 0 instead.
